t: Portugal built the first sea-borne trading empire linking Europe, Africa, Asia and the Americas, starting at Ceuta in 1415.
It controlled the spice route around Africa and became the largest national carrier in the Atlantic slave trade.
Dutch rivals, Brazilian independence and colonial wars wore it down; the last territory, Macau, went to China in 1999.
dyk: Portuguese traders who landed on Tanegashima in 1543 introduced the arquebus to Japan, where gunsmiths quickly copied it and changed Sengoku-era warfare.
ev: João I and his sons capture Ceuta, beginning the imperial project
Bartolomeu Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, opening the sea route to India
Pedro Álvares Cabral makes landfall in Brazil
King Sebastião I is killed at Alcácer Quibir, triggering a succession crisis
Brazil declares independence under Pedro I
The Carnation Revolution topples the dictatorship and opens the way to African independence

f.founder: João I, Prince Henry the Navigator
